title: FTA grants $1.28B for Utah commuter rail
summary: The 83-mile FrontRunner rail line connecting Ogden, Salt Lake City and Provo would get more trains and track, but federal funding questions could impact the project.

title: Archer Aviation to acquire eVTOL company Wisk Aero from Boeing
summary: The aircraft giant will acquire nearly 20% of Archer's Class A shares and make a future stock investment in the company.

title: Adding to Texas housing affordability challenges are soaring home insurance prices
summary: Premiums have surged 30% in Texas in the past five years, while median income has only grown 3%, a study by the Kinder Institute for Urban Research at Rice University found.

title: Steamy-hot subways are a problem in New York. They could become a clean-energy asset.
summary: An $800,000 study will examine whether subway stations’ excess heat in the summer could warm municipal buildings in colder months.

title: Transit bus orders remain strong in North America, bus manufacturer says
summary: U.S. transit agencies need to replenish their aging bus fleets, driving demand despite tariffs and uncertain future funding, NFI Group’s CEO said.

title: Cyberattack impacts critical public safety operations in California city
summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom announced a state AI cyberdefense program in the wake of the ongoing cybersecurity incident in Suisun City, California.

title: Protecting water systems from cyberattacks: 5 steps cities can take now
summary: Hacking is getting easier. But the real problem is that many systems were never designed with cyberattacks in mind, experts say.

title: Uber, Waymo go from robotaxi partners to competitors
summary: Each company plans to grow its robotaxi operations in the coming years as cities deal with regulations, lobbying and safety issues.

title: Changes to HUD homelessness aid again blocked by court
summary: The agency’s new criteria for access to $4 billion in funding for local governments to address homelessness failed to follow administrative procedures, a Rhode Island judge ruled.

title: As Flock surveillance camera backlash grows, one governor tells cities to pause installations
summary: Connecticut Gov. Ned Lamont is asking police officials to develop guidelines on surveillance technology and clarify how data is collected and used.
